documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
34M for yearly physical. Feeling good. Busy season wrapping up, a couple of 60-hour weeks in September, now easing. No lingering muscle problems since the trichinella in July, which resolved. No new symptoms.

Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Social: unchanged. Never smoker, a few beers a week.
FH unchanged (dad DM2, mom hypothyroid).

ROS: negative.

Exam: well, vitals reviewed. HEENT normal. No thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. Skin with no rashes or worrisome lesions, some sun on forearms. Muscles nontender, strength normal. No edema. PHQ-2: 1.

A/P: well adult.
- CBC and CMP today. Lipids and A1c were fine last year, will repeat A1c next year given his dad.
- Flu and covid done 10/7. Tdap current (2024).
- Back next fall, or text me sooner.

documents.title: Labs from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All normal, Glenn. Blood counts, kidneys, liver and sugar all where they should be. See you next year.

documents.title: It's back I think
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Doc, my eyes are puffy again like last summer and I'm sore all over, worse every day this week. Now I've got a rash too. Haven't been hunting. Can you see me?

documents.title: RE: It's back I think
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes. Come in at 7:30 tomorrow, I'll fit you in before my first patient. If you get short of breath or chest pain tonight, go to the ER instead.

orders.reason: trichinellosis with fever, rash and splinter hemorrhages

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Acute Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen urgently. Had trichinella last July from hunting-trip game, treated and cleared with normal labs in August.

Now: about three weeks ago had a couple of days of belly pain with nausea and vomiting that passed on its own, he chalked it up to a bug. Over the past week progressively sore muscles, legs and arms, eyes swelling again, and a rash that spread over the trunk and limbs in the last few days. Fevers at home. No travel this year, no hunting. When asked about food, he ate a pulled pork sandwich at a fair about two weeks before the stomach trouble and remembers it being pink in the middle. No SOB, chest pain or palpitations. Taking nothing but Tylenol.

Exam: T 38.3, other vitals in flowsheet. Looks tired. Bilateral periorbital edema. Diffuse rash over trunk and extremities. Splinter hemorrhages under several fingernails. Tender to palpation over thighs, calves and upper arms. Heart regular, no murmur heard. Lungs clear.

A/P: picture is trichinellosis again, a new infection from the fair pork, not a relapse of last year's. More systemic this time with the rash and nail findings, and febrile. Splinter hemorrhages fit trichinella but with fever I want cultures before calling it. Talked with the hospitalist at the regional hospital, accepted for direct admission today: labs, cultures, start treatment and steroids per them. A friend from his crew is driving him straight over.
I'll follow along.

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (400 mg) by mouth twice daily with food for 14 days
Take 2 tablets (40 mg) by mouth once daily for 7 days

documents.title: Outside fill notification
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Fill history feed shows two new fills on 6/26 from a hospital prescriber: albendazole 200 mg tabs, 2 tabs twice daily x14 days (#56), and prednisone 20 mg tabs, 2 tabs daily x7 days (#14). Looks like discharge meds. No discharge paperwork here yet. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Home
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Got out Friday. Fever's gone, eyes better, rash fading. Still sore. They gave me the same worm pills for 2 weeks and steroids for a week. Back at work light duty Monday.

documents.title: RE: Home
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good to hear. Finish both prescriptions. Once the albendazole is done, book a visit with me so we can recheck your blood counts and muscle enzyme and look at those fingernails. Front desk can set it up, or text me a day that works with your schedule.

documents.title: RE: Home
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Will do once things calm down on the job.

documents.title: Hospital records request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Still no discharge summary from the 6/23-6/26 admission. Called the hospital's medical records line, request for discharge summary and labs faxed with the release on file. They quoted 2-3 weeks.

documents.title: Discharge Summary, regional hospital, admitted 06/23/2026
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - MEDICINE SERVICE
Admission: 06/23/2026   Discharge: 06/26/2026
Referred by: primary care, direct admission.

Principal diagnosis: Trichinellosis (new infection; prior episode 2025 from wild game, treated).

History: 35 yo male, sent in by his PCP. Roughly three weeks of illness beginning with abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting that settled without treatment, then one week of progressive myalgias, periorbital swelling and a diffuse rash. No recent travel. Ate undercooked pork at a local fair about two weeks before the GI symptoms began. No home medications. NKDA. PSH tonsillectomy age 8. FH father DM2, mother hypothyroidism, sibling healthy. Never smoker, 3-4 drinks/week, construction foreman.

On admission: T 38.3 C. Periorbital edema; muscles tender on palpation; subungual splinter hemorrhages; diffuse rash.

Admission labs: WBC 12,000/mm3; Hgb 14 g/dL; eosinophils 2,000/mm3 (16%); CK 600 U/L (ref 38-174); ALT 45 U/L (ref 7-56); AST 50 U/L (ref 8-48). Blood cultures x2: no growth at 5 days.

Hospital course: started albendazole 400 mg twice daily and prednisone 40 mg daily. Defervesced by hospital day 2, myalgias and eyelid swelling improving, tolerating diet, ambulating independently. Discharged home on hospital day 4.

Discharge medications:
- albendazole 400 mg PO BID, to complete 14 days
- prednisone 40 mg PO daily, to complete 7 days

Follow-up: PCP in 2-3 weeks with CBC with differential and CK. Return for chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations or worsening weakness.

Received by fax 8/11. Filed to chart.
